The workspace is a single editable policy file, and the prefill failed by exiting left after only partial progress. I’m now anchoring the visual read to all sampled scores, observations, metrics, inherited notes, and the parent guidance; I’ll compare the available keyframe sheets before proposing any controller change.

The shared prewarm sheets are byte-identical, so I’ll inspect one as the common initial condition. The released sheets collapse to two distinct trajectories: three identical best-scoring rollouts and one slightly worse posterior-allocation variant, which is the useful controlled comparison.

The visual/metric cross-check is consistent: the fish is actively self-propelling upstream (mean x velocity `-0.0708` versus local flow `-0.0494`) but never reaches the cylinder/target corridor. After the `6.61L` closest approach it makes a large nose-up return and exits; joint 1 reaches about `33.2°`, `251°/time`, and `1592°/time²`, while joint 2 stays near `191°/time`. The posterior terminal-allocation change preserves the same topology and slightly worsens final/mean range, so it is not a recovery mechanism.

Following the skill’s required pause point, I’m recording the diagnosis and hypothesis before editing the controller. The candidate will keep the evaluated closing-leg gait and strict rearward/persistent-opening selector, then add only a smooth selector-gated joint-1 speed guard; its measurable test is lower anterior speed without sacrificing the `-4.68L` upstream leg or `6.61L` closest approach.

The policy now contains exactly one new mechanism: within the already evaluated strict terminal selector, joint 1’s speed threshold transitions from `200°/time` to `190°/time` and damping from `6` to `12`; joint 2 and the entire closing-leg controller are unchanged. I’m now distilling the completed terminal-allocation bracket into the durable guidance, including the negative boundary and the next-test criterion.

The reusable guidance now records the completed allocation bracket and its falsification boundary. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the dedicated check-runner now; while it performs the three non-CFD checks, I’ll independently inspect the final diff and parameter ownership.
